message.content:
Lions (*Panthera leo*) and zebras (*Equus quagga*, *E. grevyi* etc.) both belong to the class **Mammalia** and share a very ancient lineage as members of the order Carnivora (lion) and Perissodactyla (zebra), respectively.  

Their last common ancestor was a primitive mammal that lived during the late Cretaceous period, roughly **65–75 million years ago**, before the major radiation of modern ungulates and carnivores. This ancestral species would have been a small, generalized terrestrial mammal—likely similar to other “stem‑mammals” such as those represented by the fossil genera *Hyaenodon* or *Mesonychium*. It possessed basic features shared across all placentals (e.g., differentiated teeth, endothermy, live birth).

In short:

| Taxon | Order | Family | Approximate time since MRCA |
|-------|------|--------|-----------------------------|
| Lion | Carnivora | Felidae | >50 Ma |
| Zebra | Perissodactyla | Equidae | >50 Ma |

Thus, lions and zebras trace back to a single, basal placental mammal that existed tens of millions of years ago—a far more distant relative than many people realize!
